article.description: With a 27-game regular-season home-court winning streak on the line and their 17-point lead gone, the Los Angeles Sparks turned to their best player, Lisa Leslie, who kept the streak alive.
article.headline: Sparks sneak past Mystics, keep home streak alive
article.linkText: Sparks sneak past Mystics, keep home streak intact
article.story:
LOS ANGELES (AP) -- With a 27-game regular-season home-court winning streak on the line and their 17-point lead gone, the Los Angeles Sparks turned to their best player, Lisa Leslie, who kept the streak alive.

Leslie was fouled while shooting and made her two free throws with 17.4 seconds left to break a tie as the Sparks defeated the Washington Mystics 73-69 on Thursday night in a matchup of the leaders of the WNBA's Western and Eastern conferences.

Tamecka Dixon clinched the win when she grabbed a loose ball
from the Mystics' Coco Miller's missed 3-point shot, was fouled and made
two free throws with six-tenths of a second to play.

Leslie said the Sparks' poise and experience made the
difference.

"Any other team with a minute and something down by one might
have folded, but not us because we have the experience,'' she said.
"If we're down by three or five or we're up, we feel like we're
going to win.''

Los Angeles had trailed 69-66 with 1:25 to play when Chamique
Holdsclaw made an eight-foot running jump shot, completing the
Mystics' 10-0 run. Sparks forward Mwadi Mabika's 3-point basket 16
seconds later tied the score, Los Angeles' first points since
DeLisha Milton's lay-up exactly seven minutes earlier.

Mabika led Sparks' scorers with 20 points, while Leslie had 14 rebounds to go with her 13 points as Los Angeles (11-1) increased its winning streak to eight games.

The Sparks also extended the WNBA-record regular-season
home-court winning streak to 28 over three seasons.

Holdsclaw had 20 points and 14 rebounds for the Mystics (10-3),
whose three-game winning streak was ended.

"I was really proud of how we battled,'' Washington coach
Marianne Stanley said. "I thought we played great defense and made
it very difficult for a team that can dominate you to really get
anything going easy.''

The Sparks led 40-30 at halftime, and the Mystics didn't take a
lead until just 4:44 to play when Ashja Jones put them up 67-66
with a 3-pointer.
